source_title: SIG plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 140 and 232 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors on 29 May 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Underlying revenue fell 9.0% amid difficult markets and poor execution, Distribution underlying operating profit fell from £53.1m to £35.5m and Group underlying operating profit was £39.6m. The Group incurred £27.1m restructuring costs and described leverage and debt as too high. Pre-IFRS 16 net debt nevertheless fell from £189.4m to £162.8m, while some regional margins improved and management launched a new turnaround plan.
already_announced_exclusion: The fundamental target-operating-model restructuring in the UK, Germany and France, property closures, redundancies, consultancy work, completed disposals and closures, and the turnaround and UK branch-closure actions announced before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Broad revenue and profit deterioration, low returns, high leverage and substantial restructuring charges indicate severe pressure. Deleveraging and isolated regional improvements provide only partial quantified offsets.

source_title: SIG plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 133 and 216 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors on 10 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue increased 24% and underlying operating profit recovered to £41.4m from a £53.1m loss as the UK turnaround accelerated, but the 1.8% operating margin remained well below the 5% ambition. Free cash outflow was £124.1m, post-IFRS 16 net debt rose to £365.0m and the Group restructured its debt facilities, while profitability improved materially in the second half and several operations moved from turnaround toward growth.
already_announced_exclusion: The UK turnaround, organisational restructuring, £3.7m restructuring activities, German team changes and November 2021 debt-facility restructuring disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The operating recovery, strong revenue growth and positive profit are substantial offsets, but very weak free cash flow, increased debt, low absolute margin and continuing turnaround work leave meaningful residual pressure.

source_title: SIG plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 133 and 197 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors on 4 March 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Like-for-like revenue fell 2%, underlying operating profit declined from £80.2m to £53.1m and margin fell from 2.9% to 1.9% amid weak markets and operating underperformance. The Group recorded £8.0m net restructuring costs, including redundancies and branch closures; post-IFRS 16 net debt rose to £458.0m and free cash flow fell to £4.2m. Reported revenue rose 1%, pre-IFRS 16 net debt fell modestly and liquidity stress testing retained headroom.
already_announced_exclusion: The UK, Ireland, Germany and Benelux restructuring and productivity actions, £6.7m redundancies, branch closures and continuing UK turnaround measures disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: A sharp profit and margin decline, weak underlying demand, low free cash generation, elevated debt and multi-country restructuring indicate high pressure. Flat reported revenue, modest pre-IFRS 16 deleveraging and liquidity headroom provide partial offsets.
